messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: GPU pool saturation detected in eu-west and us-west; autoscaler hit configured pool cap; request queue growth > 3x. severity=sev2 incident created: https://redwood/internal/incidents/539876
marco: I'm on it. seeing 429 spikes from hosted-api in eu-west. dashboard shows 'request_queue_length' from 120 -> 380 over 12m. throttles up too. linking runbook: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/autoscale-gpu
olivia: Good catch. who changed autoscaler config last deploy? can we see recent commits to infra/autoscaler? @aj any deploys in the past hour?
aj: Rolling deploy of autoscaler v2 at 2026-03-15T01:10Z. I pushed a config tweak to default max_pools from 50 -> 20 for cost experiment. That config rolled to all regions via infra-rollout. Reverting now if that's the culprit.
kate: Confirming: eu-west pools at 20/20 and us-west at 19/20. We used to have 50 in eu-west for reserved backlog. We should rollback the config. @sre_lead do we want to failover traffic to dedicated standby region while rollback proceeds?
sre_lead: Hold on. Quick mitigation plan: 1) open temporary regional fallback: route low-priority traffic to eu-central standby cluster; 2) temporarily lift max_pools to 60 globally via emergency flag; 3) throttle non-SLA customers by applying token-level policy. Start with #1 and #2 in parallel.
oncall_night: I'm executing failover for eu-west low-priority routing now. Command run: `infra-router set-route --region eu-west --priority low --target eu-central-standby --dry-run=false` Logs:
```
2026-03-15T01:27:03Z router: applied route change
2026-03-15T01:27:08Z router: 72% low-priority sessions migrated
```
support_tina: Support seeing customer tickets: multiple customers reporting slow responses; two enterprise customers (acme-corp, finly) reported 5xx/429 errors. Notified account teams, message templates ready.
marco: Pushing emergency flag to lift max_pools. Command: `kubectl -n infra set env configmap/autoscaler MAX_POOLS=60 --overwrite` -> applied. Observed new pools spinning up in eu-west. pool_count eu-west: 20 -> 48 within 4m.
eng-runtime-bot: autoscaler: new pool allocation event: region=eu-west added=28 total=48. avg_startup_time=38s
olivia: Queue length dropping: 380 -> 80 in 6m. 429 rate at edge down from 4.8% -> 0.6%. Good. Keep rollback planned though.
aj: Rolling back my cost experiment. Reverting config in infra repo and starting canary roll. PR: https://redwood/internal/infra/pull/8092
sre_lead: Leaving note: do not forget to check provider quotas—we're ballooning instance counts. @kate check with cloud-ops whether this will breach spot limits in us-west.
kate: On it. Pinged cloud-ops in #vendors. Seems we have headroom for 150 more gpus for 30m; they will monitor.
marco: Customer impact summary for now: transient 10-12 minutes of elevated 429s across eu-west and us-west; two enterprise customers saw errors during peak window; emergency fallback mitigations reduced impact. We'll follow up with postmortem and action items.
support_tina: Drafting customer comms. I'll wait for final timing window before sending. ETA 20m.
oncall_night: Monitoring: autoscaler pools stable. Running health checks: `curl -sS https://hosted-api.eu-west/health | jq .` -> {"uptime":"22d","status":"ok","queue_len":72}
marco: Adding action items in incident doc: 1) revert MAX_POOLS experiment (done) 2) add guardrail to prevent <=50% reduction in max_pools via canary 3) automated alert when pool_count < baseline for 10m 4) postmortem and blameless root cause analysis 5) customer outreach led by support.
aj: Note: my change lacked a required canary gate. I'll add a pre-deploy validation that warns on >30% lower cap for production regions.
sre_lead: Agreed. Also add: runbook update to include immediate steps to lift pool caps and safe failover commands. Assign owners.
olivia: Quick follow-up: schedule a postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:30 UTC. I'll create the incident ticket and assign owners. link: https://redwood/internal/incidents/539876/postmortem
sre_lead: Final status: mitigations successful, traffic normalized. We'll keep monitoring for 2 hours. Set incident to customer-impact=partial, severity downgraded to sev3 for follow-up.
support_tina: I'll send customer notes once postmortem doc is drafted. Template: "We experienced transient throttling due to an autoscaler configuration change; mitigation actions were taken and service has returned to normal. Follow-up with root cause and action items forthcoming." :thumbsup:
marco: Thanks everyone. Good triage. Closing live handoff in 30m unless new regressions.
